reported.title: Blink timing uses 8-bit millis slice
reported.description: The sketch compares (uint8_t)millis() differences against HALF_MS=500, but an 8-bit slice wraps every 256 ms, so the 500 ms threshold is never reached and the beacon never toggles or emits ticks.

reported.title: Quiet hold does not pause blink schedule
reported.description: While quiet is held, lastSlice is continuously reset to nowSlice, so on release the full 500 ms interval restarts instead of resuming the paused schedule; the behaviour requires pausing, not resetting, the blink phase.

reported.title: Status telemetry uses blocking millis subtraction without rollover safety
reported.description: The status interval check uses now - lastStatus >= STATUS_MS with unsigned long, which is rollover-safe, but the blink logic's 8-bit slice makes the overall timing unreliable; additionally, the status print can be delayed by serial blocking, causing jitter beyond the ±120 ms tick tolerance.

truth.description: byte HALF_MS truncates 500 to 244 so blink period is too short

truth_for_judge.description: byte HALF_MS truncates 500 to 244 so blink period is too short

exposing_checks.behaviour: serial lines matching '^tick$' every 1000 ms (Rising edge every 1 s)
D12 must not toggle more than 5 times in any 2000 ms window (Blink rate cap)

judge_input.spec:
- Nav beacon LED on D12; quiet hold switch on D3 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Blink D12 with 500 ms HIGH and 500 ms LOW while quiet is released, forever.
- Print the exact line `tick` on each rising edge of the beacon (once per 1000 ms ±120 ms).
- While D3 is held LOW, force the beacon OFF and pause the blink schedule.
- Beacon must not change state more than 5 times in any 2000 ms window during free blink.
- Every 2000 ms print `nav rises=<n> quiet=<0|1>` for operator telemetry.
